# Inside the Fūjin restoration: what the marks recover
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Fūjin** is what the evidence put back.

Fūjin's mythology is grounded in the creation narratives of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, in popular Buddhist iconography, and in the visual tradition of Japanese screen painting. He is both a primordial force and a temple guardian. The wind kami are older than the name Fūjin.  In the Kojiki's birth-of-the-kami sequence, Shinatsuhiko-no-mikoto, the wind deity, is born to Izanagi and Izanami among the elemental gods that follow the making of the islands.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Fūjin
- **ASCII form:** fujin
- **Meaning:** "Wind god"
- **Domain of influence:** Wind
- **Pantheon:** Japanese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 風神
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 81 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **風神**. On the evidence, it means "Wind god".

Strip **Fūjin** to *fujin* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **u → ū** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Fūjin** lives at [/sites/fujin/](/sites/fujin/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/fujin/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/fujin/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/fujin/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Fūjin** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Wind & Atmospheric Energy** — The wind-bag on his shoulders holds every gale; when he opens it, forests tear and roofs scatter — Japan’s wind made kami.
- **Aviation & Aerospace** — He carries the winds of the world in his bag; every flight plan reads his moods.
- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Manga, anime, and games cast him as overwhelming natural force; the wind-bag is a global shorthand.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Japanese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Kojiki](/texts/kojiki/) and [Nihon Shoki](/texts/nihon-shoki/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/fujin/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
